overview: Medical dosimetrists plan radiation treatment for cancer patients. Working with radiation oncologists and physicists, they outline tumors and nearby organs on CT and MRI images, design the radiation beams and calculate doses that hit the tumor while protecting healthy tissue. O*NET rates knowledge of mathematics at 4.2 out of 5 for this job and physics at 4.15. Many start as radiation therapists, then complete a dosimetry certificate; 40% hold a bachelor's degree and 35% a post-baccalaureate certificate in O*NET data. The BLS May 2025 median is $147,470, in a small field of 3,410 jobs.
pay: Medical dosimetrists earn a median of $147,470, and pay is high even at entry: the lowest 10% earn $111,670 or more. Washington has the highest state median at $189,280, 28% above the national figure, followed by Oregon at $183,990. Texas, Florida and New York have the most jobs.

faq.q: How much do medical dosimetrists make?
faq.a: The BLS May 2025 median is $147,470 a year. The middle half earn between $132,080 and $167,030, and the top 10% earn $185,450 or more. Washington, Oregon and New Jersey ($170,650) pay the most. New York has 300 jobs at a median of $166,540.

faq.q: How do you become a medical dosimetrist?
faq.a: Most complete an accredited dosimetry program of about 1 to 2 years, often after working as a radiation therapist. In O*NET data, 40% hold a bachelor's degree, 35% a post-baccalaureate certificate and 15% a master's degree. Most employers want the CMD certification.

It can be. In O*NET data the job ranks at the top of all U.S. jobs for tight deadlines, since treatments start on fixed dates, and mistakes can have serious consequences. On the other hand, the work is indoors at a desk, ranking above 96% for sitting.

faq.q: What jobs are similar to medical dosimetrist?
faq.a: The closest are Water Resource Specialists (72% match), Nuclear Engineers (72%) and Petroleum Engineers (71%), based on O*NET 31.0. Nuclear Engineers earn $133,970, 9% less, according to BLS May 2025 data, while Computer Hardware Engineers, a 70% match, earn 10% more.
